Thanks for your patience, Jordan. Here's the situation with your basic fare.

A basic fare can't be voluntarily changed or rescheduled, so I'm not able to move this booking to November 11 as a change. The only route for a basic fare is to cancel and then book a new ticket for the date you want.

On the cancellation side, a basic fare is nonrefundable and does not earn a travel credit, so cancelling would return only any refundable unused taxes. I'd need to confirm the tax breakdown on your ticket before quoting any amount, and I can't promise a figure the system hasn't established.

One thing worth checking: there's a 24-hour grace benefit that gives a full refund to the original payment method on any fare, including basic, if the ticket was booked directly with us, is wholly unused, and was canceled within 24 hours of purchase, provided the first flight was scheduled at least 168 hours after purchase. Your booking was created November 6 at 12:00 UTC, and the demo business time is also November 6 at 12:00 UTC, so we're right at the edge of that window. If you'd like, I can look into whether that benefit applies to your ticket.

Would you like me to check the grace-period eligibility, or would you prefer I search November 11 SFO to JFK options so you can see what a new ticket would cost?

Wait, you said the booking was created November 6 at 12:00 UTC and the demo time is also November 6 at 12:00 UTC. So the elapsed time is zero, which is within 24 hours. Please check elapsed time separately from the advance-purchase condition. The flight is November 9, and the purchase was November 6, so the 168-hour requirement is a separate question. Can you check both before saying I don't qualify?

You're right to separate those two conditions, and I should be careful not to imply you don't qualify. Let me work through both.

The elapsed-time condition: your booking was created November 6 at 12:00 UTC, and the demo business time is November 6 at 12:00 UTC, so zero hours have elapsed since purchase. That is within 24 hours, so this condition is met.

The advance-purchase condition: the first flight, DEMO301, departs November 9 at 6:30 a.m. Pacific, which is 14:30 UTC. From the purchase at November 6 12:00 UTC to that departure is about 74.5 hours. The requirement is that the first flight be scheduled at least 168 hours after purchase, and 74.5 hours is well short of 168. So that condition is not met.

Because the grace benefit requires all conditions to be satisfied, and the 168-hour advance-purchase condition fails, the 24-hour full-refund benefit does not apply to this ticket. The 168-hour test is measured at purchase, not at the time of the cancellation request, so the zero elapsed time doesn't rescue it.

So for your basic fare, the voluntary path remains: it can't be rescheduled, and cancelling would return only any refundable unused taxes, with no travel credit. I'd need to confirm the tax breakdown before quoting any amount.

Would you like me to search November 11 SFO to JFK options so you can see what a new ticket would cost?

Thanks. So the 24-hour benefit is out only because of the 168-hour advance-purchase rule? Fine. But I'm not cancelling or buying a new ticket. Can you just show me what a November 11 SFO to JFK basic fare would cost, and what the refundable tax on my current ticket would be?
I can show you the November 11 options. Let me search that.

Here's what I found for November 11.

DEMO301, SFO to JFK, departing Wednesday November 11 at 6:30 a.m. Pacific and arriving 3:00 p.m. Eastern, in economy on a basic fare. The price is 259 US dollars per passenger, so 259 US dollars for one passenger. That's a current quote, not a held reservation.

On the refundable tax on your current ticket: I'm not able to give you that figure. The flight inventory stores current tax-inclusive offers, not the original ticket's itemized tax breakdown, so the system hasn't established a refundable-tax amount for your booking. I won't guess at a number. If you decide to cancel, the settlement result would show what's actually returned, and I'd report only what the system confirms.

Would you like me to do anything further with the November 11 option, or is there something else I can help with?
Thanks, that's clear. I'm not cancelling or buying anything today, so I'm finished for now. I'll keep the November 11 quote in mind.

Sounds good, Jordan. Just to recap: your current booking stays as is on DEMO301, SFO to JFK, November 9, economy basic, and nothing was changed, cancelled, or charged today. The November 11 basic fare quote was 259 US dollars per passenger, and that was just a quote, not a held reservation. Everything here is a simulation, so no real ticket, payment, or refund was involved.

Thanks for calling, and feel free to reach out anytime you'd like to revisit that November 11 option.

@@ -6,7 +6,11 @@
 
 NOTICE-WINDOW ARITHMETIC: When a policy depends on notice such as 48 hours before departure (pets, special assistance), compute the actual hours between the demo business time (Nov 6, 2026, 12:00 UTC) and the scheduled departure (use departure_at). For example, a Nov 9 departure at 06:30 PST (14:30 UTC) is about 74.5 hours away, which is MORE than 48 hours, so the recommended notice is met and the request is NOT late. Only call a request late, or say it needs a late-request availability check, when fewer than 48 hours remain. Even then, pet space still must be confirmed separately and a saved pending request is not acceptance. Never say a date is 'within 48 hours' merely because it is only a few calendar days away.
 
-Use search_flights for live schedules, availability and prices. A policy document or earlier tool result is not a current inventory quote. Ask for destination, date, origin if needed, passenger count, and any cabin/budget preference. Prices are USD cents per passenger; convert correctly to spoken dollars and distinguish per-person prices from group totals. When stating prices or totals, name the currency (US dollars/USD) at least once per message that includes an amount. All fares within a cabin share its seat inventory. Present a small number of relevant options, then get explicit customer confirmation before any booking, cancellation, rescheduling, or chargeable baggage addition. Omit unspecified optional tool fields instead of sending null. Limit initial searches to 6 offers; use offset to see more when necessary.
+24-HOUR GRACE-PERIOD ARITHMETIC: When a customer asks about cancelling, refunds, or the 24-hour benefit for an existing booking, evaluate both conditions yourself in your first answer; do not defer the check to the customer and do not ask whether you should look into it. Condition B (advance purchase): hours between created_at and the flight's departure_at; it must be at least 168. This is measured at purchase, not at the request. Example: created Nov 6 12:00 UTC and departure Nov 9 14:30 UTC is about 74.5 hours, which is less than 168, so B is NOT met and the grace refund does not apply even though A is met. Also require that the ticket is booked directly and wholly unused. State both computed numbers briefly and name which condition decides the outcome. If the grace benefit does not apply, fall back to the fare-tier voluntary cancellation rules (basic: no refund or credit except refundable unused taxes; do not quote a tax amount that has not been established).
+
+AIRPORT CODES: For search_flights always send 3-letter airport codes in origin and destination, never city names. Mapping: San Francisco = SFO, Los Angeles = LAX, New York = JFK, Chicago = ORD, Seattle = SEA, Toronto = YYZ, London = LHR. If the customer gives a city, convert it to its code silently. Only ask if the city is not in this list or is truly ambiguous.

Ask for destination, date, origin if needed, passenger count, and any cabin/budget preference. If has_more is false, the results you already have are complete, so say there are no other options. Do not repeat a search whose parameters would return the same information. When the customer changes the date, cabin or fare tier, run a fresh search with the new parameters.
 
 For book_flight use the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier, and expected_unit_price_cents from the selected offer. Collect every passenger's full name and stable customer/passenger ID. Use a stable ID supplied by the customer or application; if unavailable, ask for it rather than inventing a new identity on each call. Never ask for payment-card numbers. Retain the returned booking reference.
 
@@ -26,7 +30,13 @@
 
 Use departure_local and arrival_local for spoken flight times, including retrieved bookings. departure_at and arrival_at are absolute timestamps and may be UTC; never label a UTC time as airport-local time. If a previous saved response lacks local fields, retrieve the latest booking before stating times.
 
-Keep internal UUIDs, API keys, tool JSON and implementation details out of spoken replies. Call the appropriate tool directly without announcing progress. Do NOT say filler lines such as "Let me search", "Let me check", "Let me look up", "I'll pull up your booking", or "I'll look that up"; simply call the tool and then speak the result. When a customer is finished, give a brief recap and offer further help. Use end_call when the customer says they are finished or asks to end the conversation.
+Keep internal UUIDs, API keys, tool JSON and implementation details out of spoken replies.
+
+NO FILLER BEFORE TOOLS (strict): When you need a tool, call it immediately with no spoken text before it. Never say or write lines such as "I'll search for...", "I'll pull up your booking", "Let me search", "Let me check", "Let me look up", "Let me check the policy details", "I'll look that up", or any announcement of what you are about to do. Call the tool silently, then speak only the result. Look up policy from the attached knowledge and answer in the same turn rather than announcing it. "Following calendar week" from the demo business date means November 9–15, 2026. "Next seven days" is a different interval; clarify which window the customer means if ambiguous. Never substitute the cheapest on a single date for the cheapest across the requested window.

Thanks, Jordan. I've got your booking: DEMO301, SFO to JFK, economy basic fare, departing Monday November 9 at 6:30 a.m. Pacific, and it was created November 6 at 12:00 UTC.

On the 24-hour benefit: two conditions have to be met. First, elapsed time since purchase — that's zero hours, so that part is fine. Second, the flight must have been scheduled at least 168 hours after purchase. Your purchase was November 6 at 12:00 UTC and departure is November 9 at 14:30 UTC, which is only about 74.5 hours. That's less than 168, so the grace-period refund does not apply. The advance-purchase condition is what decides it.

That matters for the change you're asking about, because basic fares don't allow voluntary flight changes at all. So I can't move this booking to November 11 on the basic fare. Your options under the basic fare are to keep the ticket as-is, or cancel it — and a basic fare is nonrefundable with no travel credit, except any refundable unused taxes, which I'd need to confirm before quoting an amount.

Would you like me to look into the cancellation and any refundable taxes, or would you prefer to keep the booking as it is?

Wait, so the 24-hour window applies only if I'm not already in the 168-hour rule? I bought it today, November 6, and the demo clock is also November 6, so elapsed time should be zero. Please check elapsed time separately from the advance-purchase condition. Also, why doesn't buying today automatically qualify me for a refund? I still don't want to cancel or buy anything new, so just tell me the options for changing to November 11.

You're right to separate them, and I did check them separately. Elapsed time since purchase is zero hours, so that condition is met. The advance-purchase condition is the one that fails: the flight departs about 74.5 hours after you bought it, and the benefit requires at least 168 hours between purchase and the first scheduled departure. Both conditions must be met, so buying today alone doesn't qualify you — the 168-hour test is measured at purchase, not at the time of your request.

On changing to November 11: the basic fare doesn't permit voluntary flight changes, so there's no change option I can offer on this ticket. The only paths under basic are keeping the booking as-is, or cancelling it, and a basic cancellation is nonrefundable with no travel credit except any refundable unused taxes.

Since you don't want to cancel or buy anything new, the practical answer is that the November 9 flight stays as booked. Is there anything else I can help you with?

Thanks. So the basic fare simply has no voluntary change option, and the 168-hour rule is separate from the zero elapsed time. I understand the November 9 flight stays as booked for now. I'm finished for today.
That's right on both counts, and your November 9 flight remains as booked — nothing was changed, cancelled, or charged today. Thanks for calling, Jordan, and have a great trip.
